title: Work That Doesn't Cost You
outcomeStatement: By the end of this, you'll know what makes your work feel good — and what's actually been blocking you.

practices.title: Name the one you've been avoiding
practices.body: Write the task you've been putting off longest. Just the name of it, and how long it's been there. Nothing else. You'll come back to it on day 14.

practices.title: When did work last feel good? What was different?
practices.body: A real, specific occasion. Not a good week — a good afternoon.

practices.title: Make one dull task less dull
practices.body: Take something boring on today's list and add one element of play — a time limit you race, music, doing it somewhere unusual, a stupid rule. Then do it and write whether it worked.

practices.title: The smallest win available
practices.body: On the task from day 1, find the smallest piece you could finish today — not start, finish. Do that piece. Confidence comes from evidence, and evidence has to be small enough to get.

practices.behavior: write the one thing that would make today count
practices.title: One thing, before anything else
practices.body: Deciding what matters before the inbox decides for you. One line, ten seconds.

practices.title: What drains and what doesn't
practices.body: Today, notice which tasks leave you flatter than when you started and which ones don't. Same amount of work, different cost. Just mark the draining ones as they happen.

practices.title: What don't you know that's stopping you?
practices.body: Most stuckness is uncertainty wearing a costume. Find the specific unknown.

practices.title: Ten minutes, then stop
practices.body: Work on the avoided task for exactly ten minutes. Set a timer. When it goes, you're allowed to stop — genuinely allowed. Then write whether you wanted to keep going.

practices.title: Say it out loud to someone
practices.body: Tell one person what you're working on today — a colleague, a friend, a group chat. Not for accountability pressure. For the fact that work done near other people is measurably less heavy.

practices.title: The worst realistic outcome
practices.body: For the thing you're avoiding, write the worst realistic outcome — not the catastrophic one, the realistic one. Then write what you'd actually do if it happened. Fear shrinks when it's specific.

practices.title: Avoiding or resting?
practices.body: Today, notice each time you stop working and ask one question: is this rest, or is this avoidance? Both are allowed. Only one of them refuels you.
practices.noticeFor: stopping to avoid rather than to rest

practices.title: Cut one thing this week
practices.body: Find one commitment on this week's calendar you agreed to out of obligation. Cancel it, postpone it, or hand it over. Write what you cut and what you'll do with the space.

practices.cue: At a fixed hour you choose
practices.behavior: stop working — close the laptop, leave the desk
practices.title: A hard stop
practices.body: Pick the hour now and write it down. Recharging isn't what's left over after work; it's what makes the next day possible.

practices.title: That task you named on day one — where is it now?
practices.body: Done, dropped, or still sitting there. Read what you wrote on day 1, then answer honestly, and say why.
